name: Scleredema Adultorum

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Scleredema

criteria.description: Symmetrical, non-pitting induration and thickening of the skin, primarily affecting the upper back, neck, and face
Skin biopsy showing thickened collagen bundles separated by mucin deposition in the dermis
Lack of Raynaud phenomenon and negative serologic markers for systemic sclerosis
Presence of associated conditions such as diabetes mellitus or preceding streptococcal infection

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of symmetrical skin thickening with compatible histopathology and exclusion of systemic sclerosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; serologic tests help exclude mimics.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Symmetrical non-pitting induration of the skin on the upper back and neck
searchTerms: symmetrical hard skin on upper back and neck
firm skin induration on neck and back
skin thickening with hard woody feel

pathognomonic.symptomName: Facial skin involvement causing mask-like appearance
searchTerms: face skin tightening causing mask-like look
reduced facial expression from skin involvement
stiff facial skin with expression loss

common.symptomName: Limited range of motion of the neck and shoulders due to skin stiffness
searchTerms: limited neck and shoulder movement from tight skin
restricted range of motion due to skin stiffness
skin tightness causing joint movement limits

common.symptomName: Mild pruritus over affected skin areas
Associated diabetes mellitus in adult-onset cases
searchTerms: high blood sugar in adult cases

common.symptomName: History of recent streptococcal infection in acute cases

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue and malaise in acute forms
Mild dysphagia due to skin involvement of neck
searchTerms: mild swallowing problems due to skin
dysphagia related to neck skin tightness

rare.symptomName: Respiratory restriction due to skin tightness over chest
searchTerms: breathing difficulty from chest skin tightness
shortness of breath from tight chest skin

laboratory: Normal or elevated blood glucose in diabetic-associated cases
Negative antinuclear antibodies and scleroderma-specific antibodies
Elevated ESR in acute post-infectious cases
imaging: MRI may show increased dermal thickness and mucin deposition
other: Skin biopsy demonstrating thickened collagen bundles separated by mucin
Absence of vascular changes typical of systemic sclerosis

distinguishingFeatures: Vascular abnormalities and internal organ fibrosis
Presence of papular mucinous skin lesions
Histology showing dermal fibrosis without mucin

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin thickening with systemic symptoms
Development of respiratory or cardiac symptoms
Signs suggestive of systemic sclerosis or other connective tissue diseases
references: Meyer O, et al. Scleredema adultorum of Buschke: clinical and histopathological features. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2019.
Orphanet: Scleredema Adultorum. Orphanet Report Series. 2023.
LeRoy EC, Medsger TA Jr. Criteria for the classification of early systemic sclerosis. J Rheumatol. 2001.
